dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Welcome. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: Salim
dialogue.english: Fine, thank God. And how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: My name is Lina. And what's your name?

dialogue.speaker: Salim
dialogue.english: My name is Salim.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Nice to meet you, Salim.

dialogue.speaker: Salim
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مِنْ جُدَّةَ. وَأَنْتِ، مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: anaa min Juddata. wa anti, min ayna anti?
dialogue.english: I'm from Jeddah. And you, where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مِنْ مَكَّةَ، لَكِنِّي أَسْكُنُ فِي جُدَّة.
dialogue.transliteration: anaa min Makkata, lakinnee 2askunu fee Judda.
dialogue.english: I'm from Mecca, but I live in Jeddah.

pair.english: Where are you from? (to a woman)

lessons.culture: In Fusha, people greet with a full phrase such as أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا, and the standard reply to a greeting is to offer an equal or better one. Fusha is what you hear in news broadcasts, speeches and formal meetings, and it is the shared ground between speakers of different dialects.

exercises.prompt: A man says to you: 'مَرْحَبًا'. Reply warmly.
exercises.tip: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا is the standard warm reply to a greeting.

exercises.prompt: A woman asks you: 'كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟'. Answer that you are well.
exercises.tip: بِخَيْر means 'in goodness'; add الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ to give thanks.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: 'تَشَرَّفْتُ بِمَعْرِفَتِكَ'. Give a natural reply.
exercises.tip: Return the compliment with الشَّرَفُ لِي or وَأَنَا أَيْضًا.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'اِسْمِي _____.' (My name is Rami.)
exercises.tip: اِسْمِي means 'my name'; the name follows it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَنَا مِنْ مَكَّةَ، _____ أَسْكُنُ فِي جُدَّة.' (I'm from Mecca, but I live in Jeddah.)
exercises.tip: لَكِنِّي is لَكِنَّ with 'I' attached: 'but I'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'What's your name?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: مَا is 'what'; the ending كَ is 'your' for a man, كِ for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Nice to meet you.'
exercises.tip: Literally 'I was honoured by knowing you'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I'm from Jeddah.'
exercises.tip: The pattern is أَنَا مِنْ + place.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Where are you from?' when speaking to a woman?
exercises.tip: أَنْتِ with a long ee sound addresses a woman; أَنْتَ addresses a man.

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits 'كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟' most naturally?
exercises.tip: A health question gets a short answer about health.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَنْتَ / مِنْ / أَيْنَ'.
exercises.tip: The question word أَيْنَ comes right after مِنْ, and the person comes last.

dialogue.speaker: Mohammed
dialogue.english: Excuse me, can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.english: Yes, of course. What do you need?

dialogue.speaker: Mohammed
dialogue.english: I'd like some water, please.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.english: Certainly, right away.

dialogue.speaker: Mohammed
dialogue.english: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.english: From here, on your right.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.english: On your right, after the door.

dialogue.speaker: Mohammed
dialogue.english: Ah, I understand. Thank you.

pair.english: Can you help me? (to a man)

lessons.culture: Fusha has a polite opener for almost every request, and لَوْ سَمَحْتَ or لَوْ سَمَحْتِ is the one you will use most with strangers. A short شُكْرًا followed by عَفْوًا is complete and never rude.

exercises.prompt: You need help from a man. Start politely with 'Excuse me, can you help me?'
exercises.tip: Polite opener first, then the question with هَلْ.

exercises.prompt: Someone says 'شُكْرًا' to you. Reply naturally.
exercises.tip: عَفْوًا answers شُكْرًا.

exercises.prompt: A woman asks you, a man: 'لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ مُسَاعَدَتِي؟'. Reply positively.
exercises.tip: نَعَمْ is 'yes'; بِالطَّبْع is 'of course'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ سَمَحْتِ، أَيْنَ دَوْرَةُ الْمِيَاه؟'
exercises.tip: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ is the standard opener when speaking to a woman.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reply: 'شُكْرًا.' - '_____.'
exercises.tip: Keep the reply short.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Thank you very much.'
exercises.tip: جَزِيلًا means 'abundantly' and makes thanks stronger.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I want some water.'
exercises.tip: أُرِيدُ is 'I want'; بَعْضَ means 'some'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Sorry, I didn't understand.'
exercises.tip: لَمْ before a present-tense verb makes it a past negative.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'You're welcome'?
exercises.tip: عَفْوًا also means 'pardon me', depending on the moment.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'Sorry' when the speaker is a man?
exercises.tip: A woman adds ة: آسِفَة.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'مُسَاعَدَتِي؟ / تَسْتَطِيعُ / هَلْ / لَوْ سَمَحْتَ،'.
exercises.tip: Opener, then هَلْ, then the verb, then the thing asked for.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Do you have work today?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a little work.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: And tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.english: Tomorrow I'm free.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Good. Shall we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.english: Yes, of course.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Does one o'clock suit you?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.english: Yes, one o'clock is fine.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Good, I'll see you tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.english: Good, goodbye.

lessons.culture: Fusha tells the time with the feminine ordinal: السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَة, literally 'the second hour'. Plans are made with غَدًا and الْيَوْم, the same words you hear on the news.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'What time is it?'
exercises.tip: كَمِ asks 'how many', and the hour follows it.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'It's two o'clock.'
exercises.tip: Hours use the ordinal number, الثَّانِيَة, not اِثْنَان.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Today I have a little work.'
exercises.tip: عِنْدِي is 'I have' for something you have to do.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I'll see you tomorrow.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: سَ before a verb makes it future: 'I will'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'tomorrow'?
exercises.tip: Remember the three time words: الْيَوْم, الْآن, غَدًا.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'now'?
exercises.tip: الْآن is 'at this moment'; الْيَوْم is 'this whole day'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ أَنَا مُتَفَرِّغ.' (Tomorrow I'm free.)
exercises.tip: The time word can open the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَلْ تُنَاسِبُكِ السَّاعَةُ _____؟' (Does one o'clock suit you?)
exercises.tip: The hour takes الْ and the feminine ending: الْوَاحِدَة.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'هَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَفَرِّغ غَدًا؟' Reply that you are free.
exercises.tip: مُتَفَرِّغ means free of work or commitments.

exercises.prompt: Someone proposes meeting at one o'clock and asks if that works. Say yes.
exercises.tip: مُنَاسِبَة means 'suitable'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'غَدًا / سَأَرَاكَ / نَعَمْ،'.
exercises.tip: Yes first, then the verb, then the time.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.english: Excuse me, where is the market?

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.english: The market is near.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.english: Yes, go straight ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.english: And after that?

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.english: Right, and then what?

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.english: Then you will see the market on your left.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.english: Is it far?

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.english: No, it is very near.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.english: May God reward you, thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.english: You're welcome.

lessons.culture: Fusha directions use the same clear words on road signs, in news reports and in any Arab country, so a traveller is understood even where the dialect is unfamiliar. جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا is a warm thanks, and the traditional reply is وَإِيَّاكَ.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Where is the market?'
exercises.tip: أَيْنَ is 'where'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Turn right.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: يَمِينًا means 'to the right'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Turn left.' (to a woman)
exercises.tip: A woman is addressed with the ending ي: اِنْعَطِفِي.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'near'?
exercises.tip: قَرِيب and بَعِيد are opposites.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'far'?
exercises.tip: بَعِيد is the opposite of قَرِيب.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'اِنْعَطِفْ _____.' (Turn right.)
exercises.tip: Direction words take the ending ـًا: يَمِينًا, يَسَارًا.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَيْنَ _____ مَتْجَر؟' (Where is the nearest shop?)
exercises.tip: أَقْرَبُ means 'nearest'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'هَلْ هُوَ بَعِيد؟' Say no, it is very near.
exercises.tip: جِدًّا means 'very' and comes after the word.

exercises.prompt: A man has given you directions. Thank him warmly.
exercises.tip: To a woman say جَزَاكِ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا.

exercises.prompt: Ask a woman politely where the nearest shop is.
exercises.tip: Opener first, then أَيْنَ.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'مُبَاشَرَةً / ثُمَّ / يَمِينًا / اِمْشِ / اِنْعَطِفْ'.

too_formal.item: لِفْ يَمِين وَبَعْدَيْن رُوح عَلَى طُول

exercises.tip: ثُمَّ means 'then' and joins the two steps.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا عُمَر. هَذَا أَخِي كَرِيم.
dialogue.english: Hello, Omar. This is my brother Kareem.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا بِكَ يَا كَرِيم. فُرْصَةٌ سَعِيدَة.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan bika yaa Kareem. fursatun sa3eeda.
dialogue.english: Welcome, Kareem. A pleasure.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Do you have brothers and sisters, Omar?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Yes, I have two brothers and a sister.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Six people. My family is big.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: And what does your father do?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: My father works as a teacher. And yours?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أَبِي طَبِيب. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُعَرِّفَكَ بِهِ.
dialogue.transliteration: abee tabeeb. ureedu an u3arrifaka bihi.
dialogue.english: My father is a doctor. I'd like to introduce you to him.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: With pleasure. How old is your brother?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: He is eighteen years old.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Masha Allah, your family is lovely.

pair.english: How many people are in your family?

response.english: My father works as a teacher.

lessons.culture: Fusha introduces a male with هَذَا and a female with هَذِهِ, so the word itself tells you who is being presented. Arab families are large and close, and being introduced to someone's father or brother is a sign of trust. The usual reply to an introduction is فُرْصَةٌ سَعِيدَة, 'a happy chance'. مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ is said to praise something without envy.

exercises.prompt: Someone introduces his brother: 'هَذَا أَخِي كَرِيم.' Say it is a pleasure.
exercises.tip: فُرْصَةٌ سَعِيدَة is 'a happy chance'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي أُسْرَتِكَ؟' Say five people.
exercises.tip: فَرْد is 'one person'; the plural is أَفْرَاد.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَذَا _____ سَامِر.' (This is my friend Samer.)
exercises.tip: صَدِيق is 'friend'; the ending ـِي means 'my'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أُسْرَتِي _____.' (My family is big.)
exercises.tip: أُسْرَة is a feminine word, so the adjective ends in ة.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'This is my brother.'
exercises.tip: هَذَا is 'this' for a male.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Do you have brothers and sisters?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: لَدَيْكَ means 'you have'; إِخْوَة is 'siblings'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'How old are you?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: Arabic asks 'how much is your age', with كَمْ.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'brother'?
exercises.tip: أَخ is a brother and أُخْت is a sister.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'This is my friend'?
exercises.tip: صَدِيقِي is 'my friend'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'أَخِي / هَذَا / كَرِيم'.
exercises.tip: Start with هَذَا, then who he is, then his name.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'يَعْمَلُ / أَبِي / مُعَلِّمًا'.
exercises.tip: After يَعْمَلُ the job takes the ending ـًا.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: مِنْ أَيِّ مَدِينَةٍ أَنْتَ يَا عُمَر؟
dialogue.english: Which city are you from, Omar?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مِنْ دِمَشْق. وَأَنْتَ، مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ana min dimashq. wa anta, min ayna anta?
dialogue.english: I'm from Damascus. And you, where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مِنْ مِصْر، لَكِنِّي أَسْكُنُ فِي عَمَّان.
dialogue.transliteration: ana min misr, lakinnee askunu fee 3ammaan.
dialogue.english: I'm from Egypt, but I live in Amman.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: What is your nationality, then?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: My nationality is Egyptian. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: جِنْسِيَّتِي سُورِيَّة، وَأَنَا هُنَا فِي زِيَارَة.
dialogue.transliteration: jinsiyyatee sooriyya, wa ana hunaa fee ziyaara.
dialogue.english: My nationality is Syrian, and I'm here on a visit.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي مَدِينَتِنَا. هَلْ هَذِهِ زِيَارَتُكَ الْأُولَى؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan bika fee madeenatinaa. hal hadhihi ziyaaratuka al-oolaa?
dialogue.english: Welcome to our city. Is this your first visit?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Yes, it is the first.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Excellent. Where do you live in Damascus?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: I live near the market.

lessons.culture: In Fusha you ask مِنْ أَيِّ مَدِينَةٍ, 'from which city', because Arabs often name their home city or town before the country. جِنْسِيَّة is the official word for nationality on a passport and it is the same in every Arab country. A visitor is greeted with أَهْلًا بِكَ, 'you are among your own family'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'مَا جِنْسِيَّتُكَ؟' Say your nationality is Syrian.
exercises.tip: جِنْسِيَّتِي is 'my nationality'.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: 'أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي مَدِينَتِنَا.' Thank him warmly.
exercises.tip: جَزِيلًا adds 'very much' to شُكْرًا.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مِنْ أَيِّ _____ أَنْتَ؟' (Which city are you from?)
exercises.tip: After أَيّ the noun takes the ending ـٍ.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَتَكَلَّمُ _____ وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة.' (I speak Arabic and English.)
exercises.tip: The thing you speak takes the ending ـَ.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I'm from Damascus.'
exercises.tip: مِنْ means 'from'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'What is your nationality?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: جِنْسِيَّة is 'nationality'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Where do you live?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: تَسْكُنُ is 'you live'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'nationality'?
exercises.tip: جِنْسِيَّة is on every passport.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I speak Arabic and English'?
exercises.tip: أَتَكَلَّمُ is 'I speak'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'أَسْكُنُ / فِي / عَمَّان'.
exercises.tip: Verb, then فِي, then the place.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'زِيَارَتُكَ / الْأُولَى / هَذِهِ / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: هَلْ opens a yes-or-no question.

challenge.title: Meet someone new
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you meet someone for the first time, greet them, exchange names, say where you are from, ask politely for a glass of water, thank them, agree to meet tomorrow at a given hour and ask where the market is.
required_elements: a polite request with لَوْ سَمَحْتَ or لَوْ سَمَحْتِ
thanks and a reply to thanks
a plan for tomorrow with a time

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Hello. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا. بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. مَا اسْمُكَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan. bikhayr, al7amdu lillaah. maa ismuka?
dialogue.english: Welcome. Fine, thank God. What's your name?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: My name is Rami. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: The honour is mine. Where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مِنْ دِمَشْقَ. لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، أُرِيدُ بَعْضَ الْمَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: anaa min Dimashqa. law samahti, ureedu ba3da al-maa2.
dialogue.english: I'm from Damascus. Excuse me, I'd like some water.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Certainly. Here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Thank you very much. Shall we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: You're welcome. Yes, at two o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Good. Where is the market?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Turn right, and it is near.
